name: Jeu de Carte Sipa
description: Jeu de Carte Sipa (or simply Sipa) is a popular trick-taking game in Togo and across West Africa. It is a variant of the regional game 'Spar'. The game is fast-paced and revolves around the critical importance of the final trick. The ultimate goal is to win the last trick(s), specifically with a 7, which provides significantly higher points.

overview.description: Jeu de Carte Sipa (or simply Sipa) is a popular trick-taking game in Togo and across West Africa. It is a variant of the regional game 'Spar'. The game is fast-paced and revolves around the critical importance of the final trick. The ultimate goal is to win the last trick(s), specifically with a 7, which provides significantly higher points.

history.origins: Derived from 'Spar', which has roots in Dutch or Portuguese card traditions brought to the West African coast. It has adapted into a unique social game played in Togo, particularly in rural villages during the dry season.
timeline: 18th-19th Century: Coastal West African traders adapt European trick-taking games.
20th Century: 'Sipa' emerges as a distinct Togolese identity for the game.
Present: A social staple in Togo, Benin, and Ghana, often played with small stones as counters.
history.cultural: Commonly played alongside local music or during village gatherings; often associated with communal bonding.
history.evolution: The game's point system, focusing almost entirely on the 'last trick', makes it more tactical than standard high-card winning games.

setup.deck: 35 cards: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6. **Note**: The Ace of Spades is usually removed, making the King of Spades the highest spade.
setup.dealing: Dealer deals 5 cards to each player (in batches of 3 then 2). The winner of the previous hand deals next.

rules.objective: Win the final trick of the hand. If you win it with a 7, you score higher bonus points.
rules.gameplay:
1. Players must follow suit if possible.
2. Highest card of the suit led wins the trick.
3. Winner of a trick leads the next.
4. **The Last Trick**: Only the points from the last one, two, or three tricks matter.
keyRules: Must follow suit if possible; if void, play any card.
Highest card of the suit led wins the trick; winner leads the next trick.

Only the last one, two, or three tricks are scored; winning the last trick with a 7 scores 2 points, with another card 1 point; winning the last two tricks with 7s scores 4 points; all three last tricks with 7s scores 6 points.
First to reach agreed target (e.g. 10 points) wins; winner of each hand deals the next.

strategy.basic: Save your high cards (Aces, Kings) to win control of the lead in the mid-game, then lead your 7s in the final tricks when everyone else has run out of higher cards of that suit.
strategy.intermediate: Suit tracking: Pay close attention to which suits have been 'voided' by other players. If you know the person to your left is out of Diamonds, your Diamond-7 becomes a guaranteed point if you have the lead for the last trick.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Lead: If you don't have a 7, lead your highest card for the final trick to prevent an opponent from winning with their 7.
tips: The '7' is the most valuable card in the game. Don't waste it on a middle trick.
If you see someone hoarding cards of a single suit, try to force that suit out early.

scoring.description:
- **2 points**: Win the last trick with a 7.
- **4 points**: Win the last TWO tricks, both with 7s.
- **6 points**: Win the last THREE tricks, all with 7s (nearly impossible).
- **1 point**: Win the last trick with any other card.
scoring.winCondition: Win the final trick of the hand. If you win it with a 7, you score higher bonus points.
